STORY for issue #907, part 1: THE dsh CONSOLE SHOWS A REFUSED RUN READ IN BROKKR'S WORDS, NEVER "Reading the run…" FOREVER. The branch is story-907-console-refusal, checked out in this worktree at main d09297758. When you are done, the branch is d09297758 plus your commits. Do not rebase, squash, amend or merge main: the controller restacks.

THE DEFECT (measured by the controller on 2026-10-28, against the installed console and main's source alike; both are the same code):
- In the dsh web console, the run page for `upgrade-the-deterministic-covera-9e99b6bb` (alkemio's journal, 14 events) paints "Reading the run…" and never anything else.
- `brokkr inspect --run=… --json` prints 20,390,679 bytes for that run: its `run/started` manifest pins 110,209 files (#908). The console reads at most 16 MiB (`lib/host/config.js:9`, `OUTPUT_BOUND_BYTES`), so `runner.js` refuses the read: `ReadoutRefused`, "brokkr inspect printed more than the console reads".
- `lib/host/poller.js:74`, `runOf`, keeps only `.value` of `settled(...)` and drops `.refused`, so the run message carries `view: null`.
- `lib/client.js:1019`, `Run`, paints "Reading the run…" for `view === null`. Nothing tells the operator the read was refused, or why.
- The same `null` covers a run `locate` cannot find in the fleet (`poller.js:72-73`): it also paints "Reading the run…" forever.
- The controller replayed the console's own path (`brokkrOf(configFrom(env, cwd))`, `fleet()`, then `inspect()` per run) over all 17 runs in that workspace: 16 open in 100–300 ms, and only that one is refused.

THE CHANGE (extensions/dsh/brokkr-console only):
1. **The poller keeps the refusal.** `runOf` answers a refused read with Brokkr's refusal text beside `view: null`, the way the overview's queue, Muninn and day readouts already carry `{refused}` (`poller.js` `overview`, `client.js` about :331 and :373). It answers a run the fleet no longer lists with its own fact, not as a read in flight. The `snapshot` and the `run` messages both carry it.
2. **The run page paints it.**
   - A refused read shows the run's title, then Brokkr's words in full, in the console's existing error style (`bk-error`), and how to read the run outside the console: `brokkr inspect --run <id>`.
   - A run no longer listed says so.
   - "Reading the run…" remains only while a read is actually in flight.
   - The refusal clears when a later read of the same run succeeds.
3. **No other change.** Keep `OUTPUT_BOUND_BYTES` at 16 MiB: the size is #907's part 2, which awaits the operator's ruling. Make no change to what the console reads or how often, and none to Rust code, contracts/, fixtures/, policy/ or reference/.

BIND IT (Node's test runner, tests/ beside the existing ones, offline; write each test as this suite's tests are written):
- **poller:** a run whose `inspect` is refused (a fake brokkr whose `inspect` throws `ReadoutRefused` with known words) reaches the client that has it open as the refusal, in the snapshot and again after its head moves. A run absent from the fleet reaches it as not listed. Removal control: with `runOf` dropping `.refused` again, the test fails by name.
- **client:** the run page under a refused read paints the title and Brokkr's words exactly, never "Reading the run…". A later successful read paints the run.
- **The real bound:** a fake brokkr whose `inspect` prints more than `maxBytes` drives the actual runner's refusal through the poller to the painted words, so the test exercises the runner's bound and not a hand-made error.
- Every existing console test passes unchanged.

GATES:
- (cd extensions/dsh/brokkr-console && npm test)
- typos --hidden; quality/ratchet.sh files and clones; git diff --check
- If any doc changes: cargo test -p brokkr-cli --test it --locked -- doc_truth:: (timeout 590)

SIZE: about +40 production and +120 test lines.

Operator rulings:
- 2026-10-28, verbatim "yes, queue 1 and file 2 and 3" (#907, https://github.com/feedback-loop-ai/brokkr/issues/907): (1) is this story. (2), the console reading what it paints, is #907's part 2 and is not this story. (3) is #908, also not this story.
- Decision 0085 (the dsh operator console) and its ruling 5: the plugin's own tests run offline in CI on both hosts. Decision 0071 ruling 10: each readout's argv is built in one place (`lib/host/brokkr.js`). Linux and macOS only (decision 0063).

CONTENTION (NEVER message the-forge-9d, formerly the-forge-b9, or any brokkr-wt-* seat):
- #753's stories are in brokkr-store, brokkr-view and brokkr-cli's readers, and the TUI console;
- #896 is in brokkr-protocol adapters*.

No one else is in extensions/dsh/brokkr-console.

YOUR SEAT: you run on dsh (DeepSeek Flash, DeepSeek's platform), unboxed with dsh's own tools, at the operator's word (2026-10-26). Sign off every commit (`git commit -s`).

Judge duplication, ambiguity, underspecification, house alignment, coverage gaps, and inconsistency across proposal, deltas, design and tasks. Treat the realm house as the constitution. Return each finding with severity and its earliest owning artifact; zero findings is consistent.

Write `openspec/changes/<change>/design.md`. Record context, goals and non-goals, decisions with alternatives, risks, migration, and open questions. On return, revise the design and dependent artifacts so no finding is merely acknowledged.

Change location: `openspec/changes/{change}`. Archive operation: ["openspec","archive","{change}","--yes"].

# OpenSpec archive

Folding a change is the last task: run the archive operation named above,
which moves the change directory under `openspec/changes/archive/` and
folds its deltas into `openspec/specs/`. Folding also records which change
wrote which capability, so every capability the change touched carries a
`## Provenance` list.

After the archive operation, open each capability's
`openspec/specs/<capability>/spec.md` that the change touched and append
exactly one line under a `## Provenance` heading held at the end of the
file:

`- \`<archived-directory-name>\` — folded <YYYY-MM-DD>`

`<archived-directory-name>` is the directory the archive operation
created under `openspec/changes/archive/`; `<YYYY-MM-DD>` is the day it
was folded. Append only: never rewrite, reorder or remove an existing
provenance line, because standing truth accumulates and is not edited into
a different meaning. The line is a pointer, not a summary — it names the
change and nothing else, and the why stays in the change directory.

house.content:
This realm is a Rust workspace. Production code is Rust under `crates/`; the
Rust-only architecture is recorded by decision 0009. Semantic changes carry a
decision document with status `proposed` because only the operator accepts one.
Intake seats read `README.md` and decisions 0004 and 0005 before framing a
commission, along with the code and history it touches.

The frozen v1 contracts under `contracts/`, the production table at
`policy/phase-machine.json`, and `reference/` (its schemas included) are
read-only.
A contract change lands as a new version file beside the old one, never as an
edit. The evaluator corpus under `fixtures/` is also frozen and is never
regenerated, only versioned.

Tests are part of every change. Extend the suite that proves the code, run
`cargo test --workspace`, compile `recipes/self`, and leave formatting, clippy,
and the exact-coverage gate clean before reporting success.

Commit completed work with `git` using the repository's message style. Never
push.

The supported hosts are Linux and macOS (decision 0063); WSL2 is Linux. Write
no Windows-conditional code, test or evidence.

## Architecture

Decision 0071 rules how code here is shaped. Build to it, and cite its ruling
numbers in what you judge. Where a gate named below holds a rule, the gate is
the authority, and a finding it would catch is the gate's.

- **Pure core (ruling 1).** `brokkr-core` and `brokkr-view` do no I/O and read
  no clock, environment or randomness. They run no process. Pass `now`, paths
  and environment in as arguments. Effects live in the crates above core and
  view, and are journaled.
- **Enums and data, not traits (ruling 2).** A closed set is an enum matched
  exhaustively, with no wildcard arm that decides behaviour. Anything an
  operator extends is data under `adapters/`, `agents/`, `recipes/` or
  `realms.json`, validated and digested. Add a trait only for a seam whose
  contract spans several operations that must stay consistent with one
  another, reached across a process or service boundary, and name that seam
  in its doc comment. `ProducerTransport` is the one such trait today. A test
  double alone does not make a seam: a single substitutable function is a
  closure seam (`*_with`, `*_in`), which is how the house inverts a
  dependency otherwise.
- **Typed at the edge (ruling 3).** Parse wire, file and harness data once
  into a type, with `serde` and `deny_unknown_fields` where the contract is
  closed. `serde_json::Value` never goes past the edge, into state, or back
  out by string key. Never put `format!("{:?}")` in anything digested or
  journaled. A doubly-optional field or a string vocabulary is a missing enum.
- **Small functions (ruling 4).** New and changed functions stay within 100
  lines, nesting depth 5 and 7 parameters. Cyclomatic complexity follows
  the operator's 2026-09-26 ruling: a function may reach the higher of 15
  and its baseline, so a new function stays within 15, an existing one may
  change freely up to 15, and one already over 15 may only shrink.
  Production files stay within 800 lines and test files within 2,000, and a
  file already over may not grow. Add no new `jscpd` clone in production
  code, test code or data. `quality/` holds the measured baseline. Today's
  offenders carry `#[allow(clippy::…)]`, and #337 converts them to
  `#[expect(clippy::…, reason = "…")]`. Add a suppression only by a ruling,
  and remove it when you fix the function. A new suppression is
  `#[expect(…, reason)]`, never `#[allow]`.
- **Once (ruling 5).** Every fact has one home. A repeated vocabulary, skeleton
  or helper becomes one function or one table. An agent is defined once under
  `agents/`, and seats hire it by reference. A recipe that differs from another
  by a model, a seat or an entry is an `extends` overlay, never a copy. The
  agent library does not yet accept `extends`, and #360 builds it. Until then,
  a variation of an agent lives at the seat that hires it, overridden in a
  recipe overlay. It is never a second agent file that restates the first. A
  copy that must exist, such as a script a bundle pins, is held to its source
  by a test.
- **Nothing unused (ruling 6).** Add no alias, agent, contract version, flag or
  `pub` item without a consumer, and prefer `pub(crate)`. A deprecation names
  the release that removes it.
- **One derivation (ruling 7).** A fact shown on two surfaces is derived once
  in `brokkr-view`. The CLI, the TUI and `ui.html` only paint it. The engine
  never admits anything by a display-crate function.
- **Typed errors (ruling 8).** Return a `thiserror` enum whose `Display` keeps
  the operator's text. Tests match variants and pin each module's text once.
  Add no new `Result<_, String>`.
- **Tests that bind (ruling 9).** Assert exact values or variants, never
  `is_err()` alone. Show that every new test binds: a compiling mutation that
  removes the behaviour must make it fail. Restore the behaviour and record
  the failing test. Share fixtures through builders. Never change the process
  environment without a guard that restores it on unwind. A production guard
  left out because the exact-coverage gate would count it unreachable carries
  a removal-control test for the invariant that makes it unreachable, and the
  comment explaining the omission names that test.
- **The house's patterns (ruling 10).**
  - A harness is a module behind `AdapterKind`. This is the target form;
    today all five kinds share one module, and #347 and #348 build the
    split.
  - A CLI verb is a `Cmd` variant plus a handler.
  - A long parameter list becomes a parameter object.
  - Argv and mount tables are built with a builder.
  - Observing the world is split from deciding on it.
  - Never use a trait-object registry for a closed set.

Judges rate a finding against these rulings by this table, and cite the ruling
number:

- **info:** something a house gate would catch. The gate's verdict is the
  authority.
- **low:** a new or changed function over a ceiling, a rule written a second
  time, an item added without a consumer, or a `Value` carried past its edge
  within one module.
- **medium:** an untyped vocabulary that crosses crates, recipe or agent data
  copied instead of extended, a fact derived a second time on another surface,
  an error matched by its text, or a new test that cannot fail.
- **high or above:** any violation that hides a fail-open path or weakens a
  refusal. It is carried as a security finding.

A principle the implementer bent knowingly, and named with its reason in
`notes`, is still rated, and the judge carries that reason with the finding.

## Release configuration

The release manager prepares the candidate and profile patches; the operator
publishes them. Local validation is preparation work. Remote CI on the final PR
head, publication, channel updates and live-profile verification are handoff
steps, recorded as pending until their remote results exist. Historical
"live from" channel versions and old journal examples are historical facts,
not current-version references to replace.

```json
{

  "default_branch": "main",
  "tag_format": "v{version}",
  "version_files": ["Cargo.toml", "Cargo.lock"],
  "version_update": "Bump the workspace package and six path-dependency versions together. Run cargo update --workspace --offline without upgrading registry dependencies. Measure and update the witness and compose manifest digests because the engine version participates in their identity.",
  "release_notes": "docs/releases/v{version}.md",
  "handoff_directory": "docs/releases/v{version}",
  "scratch_directory": ".forge/release",

    {"name": "exact coverage", "instructions": "Run bash scripts/coverage-exact.sh in CI or host validation outside the workspace box before tagging. Boundary tests require creating a namespace, which the box deliberately refuses to nest.   ],
```

result.notes: The poller's runOf now returns a refused read as {view: null, refused: <Brokkr's text>} and a run absent from the fleet as {view: null, listed: false}; both snapshot and run messages carry either fact. The run page paints a refusal as the title, the refusal verbatim in bk-error, and 'Read it outside the console: brokkr inspect --run <id>'; when the fleet no longer lists an open run it paints 'Brokkr no longer lists this run.' instead of a read in flight. A later successful read replaces the message and so clears the refusal. Assumption: the not-listed fact is the boolean field `listed` (false), the wording above is the console's own copy, and OUTPUT_BOUND_BYTES is untouched at 16 MiB. Only the four console files changed; no Rust, contracts, fixtures, policy, reference or docs were touched, so the doc_truth and Rust gates were not applicable. Every new test was shown to fail by name: with runOf dropping `.refused`, 'a refused read reaches the open client as Brokkr's words, in the snapshot and after the head moves' and 'the runner's own output bound reaches the run page as Brokkr's refusal, not a hand-made error' failed; with the runner's overflow branch disabled, the runner-bound test failed (it then read not_json); with `listed` dropped, 'a run absent from the fleet reaches the open client as not listed, in the snapshot and after it drops out' failed; with the Run refusal branch disabled, 'a refused read paints the run's title and Brokkr's words, never reading forever, and a later read paints the run' failed; with the Realm unlisted branch disabled, 'a run the fleet no longer lists says so, not that it is being read' failed. Behaviours and files were restored after each mutation; the full suite then passed 193/193. Committed signed off as 7cca2df4125a3ee70e3d991227019721e4971101 on top of d09297758.

members.glm: Reviewed 7cca2df41 (d09297758 + 1 commit; 4 files, +139/-4, all under extensions/dsh/brokkr-console). CORRECTNESS: the change does what the framing says. poller.js runOf now carries a refused inspect as {view: null, refused: <Brokkr's words>} on both the snapshot and run messages (the established {value}/{refused} shape of queue/muninn/day) and answers a run the fleet dropped with {view: null, listed: false}; client.js Run paints the title, the full refusal in the existing bk-error class, and 'Read it outside the console: brokkr inspect --run <id>', and Realm says 'Brokkr no longer lists this run.'; 'Reading the run…' remains only while no answer has landed. The refusal clears on a later success because the success arm omits `refused` and the client replaces state.run wholesale (receive() case 'run'/'snapshot') — proven by test. No change to OUTPUT_BOUND_BYTES (16 MiB), read frequency, argv construction (brokkr.js untouched, ruling 10), Rust code, contracts/, fixtures/, policy/ or reference/. TESTS BIND, verified by mutation: dropping `.refused` from runOf fails 'a refused read reaches the open client as Brokkr's words…' by name (and the real-bound test); dropping `listed: false` fails 'a run absent from the fleet…'; deleting the Run refusal branch fails 'a refused read paints the run's title…'; deleting the unlisted note fails 'a run the fleet no longer lists says so'. Each mutation was reverted; tree clean. The real-bound test drives the actual runner (stub prints 8193 bytes over maxBytes 8192 → runner overflow → jsonOf ReadoutRefused 'brokkr inspect printed more than the console reads') through the poller to the painted words — not a hand-made error. Existing tests are untouched (zero deleted lines); full suite 193/193 pass offline. GATES: npm test 193 pass; typos --hidden clean; quality/ratchet.sh files and clones hold; git diff --check clean; no docs changed so doc_truth is not owed. Commit is signed off. No security smell from this seat: the refusal is painted as a React text child (escaped), the bound is unchanged, no new read, egress or fail-open path. RESIDUALS (both info, neither a return): (1) [ruling 4, info] lib/client.js grew +7 to 1746 lines, already far over the 800-line production ceiling before this story; the gate that holds that rule (quality/ratchet.sh files) scopes Rust crates/ only and its verdict holds, and the defect lives in the run-page component this file owns — recorded for the operator, since no gate measures the plugin's file sizes. (2) [info, framing-pinned] The hint is painted exactly as the story pinned it, 'brokkr inspect --run <id>'; in a many-hearth world whose realms name journals other than the world's default journal, the bare verb would not find the run where the console's own read adds --db=<journal> (brokkr.js runOf). Fine where the map's journal is the run's; if the operator wants the journal named in the hint, that is a later story. No other findings: runOf stays small (ruling 4), the refusal reuses the house's one vocabulary and existing CSS classes (ruling 5), every new field has a consumer (ruling 6), Brokkr's words are carried once and parsed nowhere twice (rulings 3/7), tests assert exact values and removal controls are recorded (ruling 9), and the new test helpers follow the suite's existing per-file mount-and-open convention rather than adding a new clone the suite does not already write.

result.notes:

Refusals survive snapshot and run messages, render as React text with the title and CLI hint, and clear when a successful read replaces state.run. Removed fleet entries carry and paint the not-listed fact. The actual runner-bound integration test reaches the painted refusal. The 16 MiB bound, read cadence, argv construction, Rust and frozen material are unchanged (0071 rulings 8-10; 0085 rulings 3-5).
Surviving findings:
